page_hint: Appendix A, §1 DeepSeek-V4, 'What this means for the architect'
quoted_clause: the constant factor itself can be cut ~10–14× across the V4 variants (the ~14× end is V4-Flash's ~7%-of-V3.2 single-token KV, §5) through attention re-architecture alone — the parameter count is unchanged, so the saving is architectural, not a smaller model.
observed: The sentence claims parameter count is unchanged while attributing the reported FLOP/KV reductions to attention re-architecture alone. The same section states V4-Pro is 1.6T and V4-Flash is 284B, so parameter count is not unchanged across V4 variants; a V4-Flash comparison to V3.2 may also involve a different total model size.
evidence: Chunk: 'V4-Pro is 1.6 T total / 49 B activated, V4-Flash 284 B / 13 B activated'. The quoted clause says 'across the V4 variants' and 'parameter count is unchanged'.
root_cause: Conflation of per-variant vendor-relative efficiency ratios with a single unchanged-parameter comparison; editing compression.
correction: Rewrite to distinguish variant sizes and vendor-relative baselines, e.g. 'For each variant, the vendor reports a reduction relative to its stated V3.2 baseline; the V4 variants themselves have different total parameter counts (1.6T Pro vs 284B Flash), so do not infer that the saving is independent of model size across variants.' Remove 'parameter count is unchanged' unless supported for the specific comparison.
acceptance_test: No sentence claims parameter count is unchanged across V4 variants; the text distinguishes variant sizes and vendor-relative baselines.

quoted_clause: Before selecting patterns, the architect reads the capstone's workload against Fig 26.1 — short prompt, latency-sensitive, moderate quality — and consults the §26.2.1 matrix, which points to the cache + breaker combination.
observed: The capstone is explicitly a distinct short-prompt workload, not the canonical 9.2K RAG case. Fig 26.1's described families are long-context RAG Q&A (context-heavy, latency 0.40), chat (traffic/latency-sensitive, long outputs), and batch (cost-sensitive, latency-tolerant). None matches 'short prompt, latency-sensitive, moderate quality' RAG, and the matrix has no row that points to semantic response cache + circuit breaker for that fingerprint.
evidence: §2.1 provenance note: 'RAG Q&A is quality- and context-heavy with short outputs; chat is traffic- and latency-sensitive with long outputs; batch inference is cost-sensitive and latency-tolerant.' Matrix rows list strategies; no cache+breaker row for short-prompt RAG. Step 1: 'The capstone declares a distinct short-prompt workload — it is not the canonical 9.2K-input/1.08-s-prefill case of Ch 4.'
root_cause: The capstone's workload was changed to a short-prompt case but the fingerprint/matrix reference was not updated.
correction: Either add a 'short-prompt RAG / support' row to the matrix and include its fingerprint in Fig 26.1, or reword Step 0: 'The capstone is a new short-prompt RAG workload; use the matrix's method to locate its dominant constraint (latency/queueing under the TTFT SLO), which motivates evaluating response caching and load shedding, rather than claiming the existing matrix points to that combination.'
acceptance_test: The reader can trace the capstone's stated fingerprint to a matrix row or to an explicit method step; no claim that an existing row points to cache+breaker unless such a row exists.

quoted_clause: the same table is carried in the archetypes are reference points, not measured clusters. **Because each bar is an author-chosen input, the bar values are [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION]; only a value computed *from* them (e.g. a ratio of two bars) would be [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED].** [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION]]).
observed: The sentence is ungrammatical ('carried in the archetypes are') and the label block ends with an extra closing bracket and parenthesis.
evidence: The quoted text contains 'in the archetypes are' and '[ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION]]).' with mismatched brackets.
correction: Rewrite as: 'The same table is carried in the figure; the archetypes are reference points, not measured clusters. Because each bar is an author-chosen input, the bar values are [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION]; only a value computed from them (e.g., a ratio of two bars) would be [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED].' Remove the extra ']' and unmatched parenthesis.
acceptance_test: The paragraph parses grammatically and all bracketed labels are balanced.

quoted_clause: the explicit caveat is that one replica's fixed <5% per-request claim stays an untested scenario hypothesis, not a basis for refusal.
observed: The phrase 'fixed <5% per-request claim' is not defined in the visible chunk. Earlier Pattern A says adding a second host 'changes per-request latency by a small amount' but does not state <5%.
evidence: Pattern A: 'adding a second host and load-balancing requests across two replicas changes per-request latency by a small amount; this is an untested scenario hypothesis...' No <5% appears.
root_cause: Stale or compressed reference to an earlier quantitative claim that was removed or not stated.
correction: Replace with a defined phrase, e.g. 'the earlier small per-request latency-change claim (if quantified, e.g., <5%, must be stated as an untested scenario hypothesis)' or remove the <5% reference.
acceptance_test: Any percentage referenced is defined in the same section or explicitly cross-referenced; no orphan '<5% per-request claim'.

quoted_clause: $ per query (marginal generation work; DERIVED from FACT inputs, §5 — not itself a FACT)
observed: In this chapter, §5 is 'Common Mistakes', which does not define the cost derivation or FACT inputs. The cost-basis rules are discussed in §4 Measurement and §26.8 (referenced elsewhere in the same table/footnote).
evidence: Chapter headings: '## 5. Common Mistakes'; Table footnote: 'see §26.8'; §4 defines FACT set.
correction: Change '§5' to the section that defines the cost derivation, likely '§4' or '§26.8', e.g. 'DERIVED from FACT inputs, §4/§26.8'.
acceptance_test: The reference resolves to the passage that defines marginal-generation-work cost and FACT inputs.

quoted_clause: vLLM's widely cited 54% is a decode inter-token-latency slope from its Llama-3.1-8B Table 3 — a latency metric, not a memory ratio; there is no vendor-measured FP8 memory footprint, and any allocator block/metadata overhead is not vendor-measured.
observed: This is a specific bibliographic/technical claim (vLLM, Llama-3.1-8B, Table 3, 54%) but the chunk provides no citation or source for it. The absolute phrase 'there is no vendor-measured FP8 memory footprint' is also broad.
evidence: No vLLM source is listed in the adjacent text or First-hand Sources for this claim.
root_cause: Unsupported or under-cited empirical claim; overgeneralization.
correction: Add a precise citation to the vLLM source and scope the claim, e.g. 'In the cited vLLM evaluation, the 54% figure is an inter-token-latency result for a specific model/configuration, not a memory ratio; do not treat it as a vendor-measured FP8 KV footprint.' Soften 'there is no vendor-measured...' to 'the cited source does not provide a vendor-measured FP8 KV footprint'.
acceptance_test: The 54% claim has a verifiable source and is scoped to the cited evaluation; no unqualified universal negative.

page_hint: Appendix A, 'This is a dated field guide' and A.10 First-hand Sources
quoted_clause: Reproduction status is recorded per family in the First-hand Sources list (A.10): each entry carries its source URL/identifier, the version and release date where known, and the verification status (whether the claim is vendor-reported [1P] pending independent check, or independently verified).
observed: The visible A.10 entries do not carry per-family verification status or, in several cases, release dates; they only list sources and a general compiled note.
evidence: A.10 list: DeepSeek entry has no release date or verification status; Kimi entry has no release date or verification status; Qwen entry has no release date or verification status; GLM entry has date but no explicit verification status.
root_cause: Overstated description of the source list.
correction: Either add the claimed fields to each A.10 entry (version/release date where known, verification status) or reword: 'The First-hand Sources list records the source identifiers; the general compiled note states that all parameters/claims are vendor-reported [1P] and require verification on the architect's own hardware.'
acceptance_test: The text's description matches the actual A.10 entries.

quoted_clause: circuit breaker activation reduces tail latency for remaining requests by 35% because the system sheds load before the model queue fills.
observed: The 35% reduction is a specific quantitative effect but is not derived from any stated queueing model; it is labeled [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION], yet the causal 'because' can make it read as a mechanism-level expectation.
evidence: No calculation in the chunk derives 35%; it is a scenario input.
root_cause: Quantified assumption presented with causal language.
correction: Reword as 'In this scenario, assume circuit-breaker activation reduces tail latency for remaining requests by 35%; this is an input to be measured, not a derived effect.' Or remove the percentage until a queueing model supports it.
acceptance_test: The percentage is clearly an assumed scenario input, not a derived or generally expected effect.

quoted_clause: These components sum to a ~450 ms baseline TTFT budget, which the capstone declares as the baseline p99 scenario value (a scenario input, not a derived quantile of a distributed sample; a real baseline p99 must come from a measured latency distribution). The 450 ms is a service-time sum with no queueing term; at the offered ~2 rps against the ~2.0 req/s analytical ceiling (ρ near 1), a real queueing delay sits on top
observed: The text calls 450 ms a 'baseline p99 scenario value' while also stating it is a service-time sum with no queueing term and that at ρ near 1 a real queueing delay sits on top. This can mislead readers into treating a service-time sum as a p99 latency.
evidence: The quoted sentence itself distinguishes service-time sum from measured p99.
root_cause: Terminology overload: 'p99 scenario value' used for an assumed service-time target.
correction: Change to 'baseline service-time target' or 'assumed baseline p99 service-time component' and keep the warning that a real p99 must include queueing.
acceptance_test: The 450 ms is not labeled a p99 unless it is explicitly an assumed p99 service-time component, and the text says real p99 includes queueing.

quoted_clause: it reports 3.0× less attention compute and a 4.4× smaller KV cache

evidence: The adjacent text says the measures are normalized per-head/per-layer and are not whole-model ratios, so precise wording matters.
correction: Use '3.0× lower attention compute' or 'attention compute reduced by a factor of 3.0' (if that is the vendor's intended ratio).
acceptance_test: No '× less' phrasing remains in the GLM comparison.

quoted_clause: A typical re-sizing that lets the peak load concentrate on the canonical fleet would have to be computed under §26.8's cost-basis rules — §26.8 states those rules but does not perform the re-sizing — and it is not a 48% figure
observed: The phrase 'lets the peak load concentrate on the canonical fleet' is unclear; re-sizing normally changes fleet size to absorb or distribute load, not to concentrate it. The sentence is hard to parse and may misstate the excluded calculation.
evidence: The surrounding text discusses fixed fleet and re-sizing; no definition of 'concentrate' is given.
correction: Rewrite as: 'Any re-sizing that would allow the canonical fleet to absorb the peak load at a lower all-in cost would have to be computed under §26.8's cost-basis rules; §26.8 states those rules but does not perform that re-sizing, and it is not a 48% figure.'
acceptance_test: The sentence clearly states what re-sizing is being excluded and why.
